topic: Modes of Nutrition and Reproduction in Fungi
title: How Does Bread Mould Spread? Explained Simply | PUC Biology Class 11
description:
Diya leaves bread out for four days, and the green-black mould jumps to the next slice without touching it. How? To answer that, this lesson asks two questions: how does a fungus eat, and how does it make more of itself?

A live zoom ladder takes the mould on Diya's bread down to its mycelium, rhizoids, a sporangium and the spores that float to the next slice (Rhizopus). Then the three modes of nutrition (saprophyte, parasite like Albugo and Puccinia, symbiont as lichen and mycorrhiza), the three routes of reproduction (vegetative, asexual spores, sexual spores), and the sexual route animated step by step: plasmogamy, the dikaryon (n + n), karyogamy and meiosis. Asexual vs sexual spores side by side, a worked example on the sexual cycle of Agaricus, the exam trap on plasmogamy and karyogamy, an original NEET pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

This is Episode 16 of our PUC Biology series.
Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11 and NEET students.
